facts.fact_text: On 25 March 2003, the applicant and others held the picket in front of the Sverdlovsk Regional Court.

During the picket on 25 March 2003, the applicant and others distributed press clippings and leaflets about Mr Ovcharuk, the President of the Sverdlovsk Regional Court, who had allegedly been involved in corruption scandals.
During the picket on 25 March 2003, the applicant and others collected signatures for the dismissal of Mr Ovcharuk, the President of the Sverdlovsk Regional Court.

Witnesses Mr M. and Mr R. testified that at about 9.10 a.m. on 25 March 2003 they had gone onto the porch of the Sverdlovsk Regional Court and seen some people with banners, among them Mr Kuznetsov (the applicant) holding the banner 'Ovcharuk – resign'.
Witnesses Mr M. and Mr R. testified that the picket participants were standing on the porch right in front of the entrance on the top floor, blocking the passage and distributing leaflets.

Witnesses Mr M. and Mr R. testified that when they asked the picket participants to show their identity documents and go down the stairs, the participants refused, but went down after a police officer approached them.
Witnesses Mr M. and Mr R. testified that judges coming to work had told them that the picket participants had blocked access to the Sverdlovsk Regional Court.

On 17 April 2003, an official of the Verkh-Issetskiy police department of Yekaterinburg compiled a report on administrative offences committed by the applicant under Article 20.2 §§ 1 and 2 of the Code on Administrative Offences.
According to the report of 17 April 2003, the applicant had given notice of the picket too late.
According to the report of 17 April 2003, the applicant had distributed leaflets of a slanderous and insulting nature against the president of the Sverdlovsk Regional Court.
According to the report of 17 April 2003, the applicant had obstructed the passage of citizens into the court-house of the Sverdlovsk Regional Court.

On 19 May 2003, the justice of the peace issued a ruling on an administrative offence (постановление по делу об административном правонарушении) in which she found the applicant guilty on three counts.
The justice of the peace held that the applicant had breached the established procedure for organising a picket by sending the picket notice eight days before the picket date.
The justice of the peace held that both the 1988 USSR Supreme Council's Decree and the local Yekaterinburg regulation on public assemblies established a ten-day notification period for pickets.
The justice of the peace found the applicant guilty of breaching public order during the picket, relying on the report on an administrative offence dated 17 April 2003.
Witnesses Mr M. and Mr R. testified in court that they worked as court bailiffs in the Sverdlovsk Regional Court.
The justice of the peace relied on the report by court bailiff Mr R. of 25 March 2003 as evidence of the applicant's guilt.

The justice of the peace relied on the report by police officer Mr G. from the Verkh-Issetskiy police station, which indicated that between 25 and 28 March 2003 he had been responsible for public order during the picket in front of the Sverdlovsk Regional Court.

Police officer Mr G.'s report stated that the picket had been organised by Mr Kuznetsov (the applicant), Mr Sh., and Ms M., who at 9 a.m. on the day of the picket were standing on the staircase at the entrance to the Sverdlovsk Regional Court and thus obstructing access to the building.

Police officer Mr G.'s report stated that following his intervention and that of the court bailiffs, the picket participants went down to the pavement in front of the court-house and did not subsequently interfere with the normal functioning of the Sverdlovsk Regional Court.
The justice of the peace declared the applicant guilty under Article 20.2 §§ 1 and 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The justice of the peace fined the applicant 1,000 Russian roubles (approximately 35 euros).
On 11 July 2003, the Verkh-Issetskiy District Court of Yekaterinburg, on an appeal by the applicant, upheld the ruling of the justice of the peace.
The Verkh-Issetskiy District Court of Yekaterinburg endorsed the reasons given by the justice of the peace in upholding the ruling.

Under section 2 of the Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988, organisers of an assembly were required to give written notice to the municipal authorities no later than ten days before the planned assembly.

Under section 3 of the Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988, the municipal authority was required to give its response no later than five days before the assembly.

Under section 4 of the Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988, assemblies were to be conducted in accordance with the aims listed in the notice and with respect for Soviet laws and public order.

Under section 8 of the Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988, individuals who breached the established procedure for organising and holding assemblies incurred liability under the laws of the USSR and Soviet republics.

Article 20.2 § 1 of the Code on Administrative Offences provides that a breach of the established procedure for organising a demonstration, meeting, procession or picket shall be punishable by a fine of ten to twenty times the minimum monthly wage, which was 1,000 to 2,000 Russian roubles at the material time.

Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code on Administrative Offences stipulates that a breach of the established procedure for holding a demonstration, meeting or picket shall be punishable by a fine of ten to twenty times the minimum wage for organisers, or five to ten times the minimum wage for participants.
